synopsis: The corpus explicitly identifies both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty in stochastic radar detections, for which mean and RMSE errors alone are inadequate; it recommends distribution-level validation when individual sensor returns cannot meaningfully be matched one-to-one [f4821, f4801]. Across the safety case, sensor, operator-response and machine-response uncertainties should remain separate, and the illustrative two-second operator/mechanical delay must not be treated as a validated population distribution or percentile [f3504, f11830, f3475]. Stopping predictions and braking escalation should use uncertainty-bounded stopping margins, while ground-truth measurements need independent uncertainty budgets and an explicit unavailable or ambiguous state [f6210, f6280, f5394, f7473]. Credibility requires physical anchors, a stated validity envelope and explicit uncertainty, rather than simulation run count; the proposed programme claim is therefore bounded by machine configuration, operating envelope, safety-function scope and residual uncertainty [f11325, f10884, f9724]. Important gaps remain: few sensor-realism studies report uncertainty bands, unknown exposure distributions can destabilize rare-event reweighting, and active-learning uncertainty estimates can themselves be wrong [f4838, f6852, f6862]. Planning should communicate numeric ranges rather than blanket contingency or verbal hedges, while treating absent correlation metrics by the first quarter of 2027 as an early credibility warning; uncertainty graphics are not guaranteed to improve trust [f9641, f9863, f9474, f11006, f9892].
